evidence.note: Triton final kernel failed to compile; agent root-caused it to tl.dot requiring matrix dims >=16 (BLOCK_M was 8) and applied the targeted fix rather than guessing.
N=2048 illegal memory access; hypothesized 32-bit offset overflow in Triton index arithmetic and fixed with int64 offsets — a genuine root-cause diagnosis of a numeric/indexing bug.

Profiled stages, identified the final Triton kernel recomputing hidden LayerNorm per D-block as the D=384 bottleneck, then deliberately redesigned to compute LN*sigmoid once and use cuBLAS linear — perf failure root-caused and design revised.

Distinguished correctness from performance failures: BF16 intermediates, fused input projection, and contraction-only BF16 all failed correctness and were reverted from backups; Triton contraction and strided GEMMs failed on speed and were rejected as non-improvements.

Revisited an earlier-abandoned input-LayerNorm Triton idea and got it working with correctness preserved, then did targeted block-size tuning keeping only correctness-preserving gains — sustained, evidence-driven correction without regressing prior wins.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed the true cause of distinct failures — a compile constraint, an int64 offset overflow, a per-block LayerNorm recomputation bottleneck — and revised the design deliberately, cleanly separating correctness failures (BF16, fused input) from performance dead-ends (Triton contraction, strided GEMM) and reverting each via backups without losing prior wins, which squarely matches anchor 8. It shows some anchor-10 traits (sustained correction across multiple failures, revisiting the earlier input-LN decision), but the numeric/Cauchy failures were reverted rather than deeply root-caused into a mitigation, and it never demonstrated knowing when to stop chasing the over-budget N=2048 shape, keeping it below a 9-10.
